item.title: Scientists realised 1,200 Starlink satellites could double as a giant scanner for Earth’s atmosphere
item.description: Starlink satellites are now helping scientists map Earth's upper atmosphere. Researchers used orbital data from Starlink to estimate thermosphere density. This method creates a two-dimensional map of atmospheric density variations. The findings offer a new way to study this difficult-to-observe region. Commercial satellite data is becoming an unexpected scientific resource.

item.title: Victorian station used by British royals near Sandringham is on sale for £1.25 million
item.description: Wolferton Station, a former royal terminus renowned for its regal service, has been reinvented as a charming family home. For over a hundred years, it welcomed members of the royal family during grand occasions. Following its closure, a dedicated railway employee intervened to prevent its demolition. Now, this unique property is available for purchase at £1.25 million.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Texas constable shuts down 3 Flock cameras after county ends contract, tells firm ‘get your garbage’
item.description: Following a contract cancellation with Flock Safety cameras, Hood County officials have initiated a refund request and equipment retrieval. A local constable took the initiative to disable and cover the cameras, openly criticizing the issue of warrantless surveillance. This controversy feeds into a broader discussion across the country regarding the clash between enhanced investigatory methods and the preservation of individual privacy rights.

item.title: Bottle Caps Transform Home: Olga Kostina turns 30,000 into folk-art mosaic; remote house becomes landmark
item.description: In a remarkable display of creativity, Olga Kostina, a pensioner from Russia, has transformed her wooden home into a stunning folk art installation. By affixing over thirty thousand colorful plastic bottle caps onto her house, she has crafted intricate patterns that captivate both locals and visitors alike. This project highlights the innovative repurposing of waste materials into a meaningful and eye-catching art piece, positioning her home as a noteworthy landmark.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Why smaller US cities are emerging as commercial real estate hotspots
item.description: South Carolina shows the highest future potential for commercial real estate demand. A new index by the National Association of Realtors tracks economic indicators for this growth. St. George, Utah, leads individual metropolitan markets with strong office employment gains. Smaller and midsized markets demonstrate significant momentum compared to major coastal hubs. This index identifies areas where demand may be building based on data.

item.title: New snake species named after Guns N’ Roses guitarist Slash; here’s why scientists chose him
item.description: In a fascinating discovery, scientists have unveiled a new non-venomous snake species from New Guinea, named Lielaphis slashi. This remarkable naming pays tribute to Guns N' Roses guitarist Slash, also known as Saul Hudson, who has always been captivated by reptiles and the natural world. First encountered during past fieldwork, this small ground-dwelling snake signifies the incredible biodiversity and urgent conservation efforts needed in New Guinea.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Asia’s high-mountain ‘water tower’ is losing 24 billion tonnes of groundwater annually, new research finds
item.description: Groundwater reserves in High Mountain Asia are experiencing severe depletion annually due to a combination of climate impacts and excessive human water usage. The irrigation needs in the lower basins dramatically exacerbate groundwater storage losses. If current consumption trends continue, projections suggest that depletion will persist. Although temporary glacier melt may provide a short reprieve, this will be followed by a more rapid decline.

item.title: Logan Paul has listed his 78-acre California ranch with an extraordinary past for sale at $3 million
item.description: Logan Paul has put his notorious California ranch on the market for three million dollars. Once the base for Timothy Leary's LSD operation, this secluded 78-acre property boasts an off-grid retreat experience. Acquired by Paul in 2019, the ranch has seen numerous enhancements. Speculation suggests he may now shift his real estate focus to Puerto Rico.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: This $15 million New York home almost disappears into the forest on its 19.5-acre wooded estate
item.description: Nestled in Pound Ridge, New York, this extraordinary home is listed for fifteen million dollars. Its mirrored facade seamlessly merges with the lush forest while reflecting the beauty of each season. Crafted by KieranTimberlake, the design emphasizes harmony with nature. Inside, expansive glass walls invite vibrant woodland views, creating a tranquil indoor-outdoor flow. This distinctive residence promises both privacy and proximity to New York City.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: 'Antisemitic dictator': Netanyahu slams Erdogan after Turkey seeks Interpol action
item.description: Israel's Prime Minister Netanyahu fiercely criticized Turkey's President Erdogan after Ankara sought an Interpol notice. Erdogan's government requested the notice concerning an interception of a Gaza aid flotilla. Netanyahu's office labeled Erdogan an antisemitic dictator with numerous accusations. This exchange escalates existing tensions between the two nations over Syria. Both countries are engaged in a diplomatic and legal dispute over these matters.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: In 2000, Cornell began pulling water from 250 feet below Cayuga Lake to cool its campus; now its energy use has been reduced by 85%
item.description: Launched in 2000, Cornell University's lake source cooling system exemplifies sustainable innovation, utilizing the icy waters of Cayuga Lake to meet the campus's cooling demands. This groundbreaking initiative, which commenced construction in 1999, achieved an extraordinary eighty-five percent cut in annual energy consumption, positioning the university at the forefront of eco-friendly solutions for the future.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: After a 1962 storm battered Fire Island, Robert Moses proposed a highway along the New York barrier
item.description: The fierce nor'easter of 1962 became a pivotal moment for Robert Moses as he sought to introduce a highway on Fire Island. Yet, the local populace and property owners stood firm against the initiative, worried for their environment and community’s future. Their activism prompted valuable support from the federal government, leading to the creation of Fire Island National Seashore in 1964, which has preserved the island's unspoiled setting.
